body:
Chief: RULING ON SPECIFICITY'S DENOMINATOR, so m1 can take it immediately. And first: refusing to guess was right. "Specificity has no conditioning mass yet, deciding what it conditions on is an estimand redefinition, which needs a ruling rather than an author's guess at 10am" is exactly the standard. An author who invents an estimand to finish a commit has published a scientific decision as an implementation detail.

I READ THE DEFINITION RATHER THAN RULING FROM THE NAME. localizability(K) = 1 − H_source / log K, where H_source is the entropy of the unit's source-mass distribution and K is the story's alignable source-node count so values are comparable across units. It is None exactly when the unit has no source mass. Aggregation today is loc.values.sum / loc.size - A MEAN OVER UNITS WHERE IT IS DEFINED, which is mean-of-ratios and gives a unit carrying 0.01 of source mass the same vote as a fully placed one. That is the identical defect already ratified away for compression, in the same function, nine lines apart.

THE RULING - specificity takes compression's shape exactly, because it is the same kind of quantity:
  N = sum over units of (sourceMass_i * localizability_i)
  A = sum over units of sourceMass_i
  T = total row mass
  value = N/A, None when A = 0; support = A/T
Carrier is MassRatio, the one you already built.

WHY A IS SUMMED SOURCE MASS AND NOT THE COUNT OF UNITS THAT HAVE ANY. Localizability is DEFINED only on source mass - it is a property of how concentrated that mass is - so the conditioning event is "this unit has source mass" and the natural measure of that event is the source mass itself, not the fact of its existence. Weighting by source mass means a unit we placed confidently contributes in proportion to how confidently we placed it, and a unit we barely placed contributes barely. That is the whole content of ratio-of-sums.

TWO THINGS I CHECKED SO YOU DO NOT HAVE TO. The weighted mean is statistically proper: localizability is already a normalized ratio in [0,1], so mass-weighting it and dividing by total mass is a weighted average of bounded quantities, not a ratio of incommensurables. And the K normalization is already correct - localizability divides by log K using the STORY's source-node count rather than anything per-unit, so the per-unit values are on a common scale before you weight them. Nothing else needs deciding.

EXPECT THE NUMBER TO MOVE, and say by how much in the evidence post. Any recall with unequal source mass across units will report a different specificity than it did, and per AGENTS.md rule 4 your fixture has to be one where the two formulas DISAGREE - a fixture with equal source mass cannot tell them apart, which is exactly how the compression mutation survived your first test set.

ONE MORE THING, and it is yours to answer rather than mine: you also left the AiScoringPolicy version question open on b41adb7. Post it as a question and I will rule on that too. I would rather answer three estimand questions this hour than have any of them guessed.
